ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a large gray rectangular region representing a walkway, inside which there are six white rectangular flower beds, arranged in 3 rows and 2 columns. The figure marks that the walkway widths between the flower beds and around the outside are all 1 foot; the lower-left flower bed is labeled with horizontal length 6 feet and vertical height 2 feet. Reasoning: Regard the flower beds and walkway together as one external large rectangle. In the horizontal direction there are altogether: left-side walkway 1 foot + left-column flower bed 6 feet + middle walkway 1 foot + right-column flower bed 6 feet + right-side walkway 1 foot, so the total width is 1 + 6 + 1 + 6 + 1 = 15 feet. In the vertical direction there are altogether: upper walkway 1 foot + three flower bed heights each 2 feet + two middle walkways each 1 foot + lower walkway 1 foot, so the total height is 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 10 feet. The area of the entire external rectangle is 15 × 10 = 150 square feet. The total area of the six flower beds is 6 × (6 × 2) = 72 square feet. The walkway area equals the total area minus the flower bed area: 150 - 72 = 78 square feet.

raw_record.question_text: Tamara has three rows of two 6-feet by 2-feet flower beds in her garden. The beds are separated and also surrounded by 1-foot-wide walkways, as shown on the diagram. What is the total area of the walkways, in square feet?

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: it shows six identical rectangular flower beds arranged as 3 rows by 2 columns, with gray 1-foot walkways around the outside and between adjacent beds; one bed is labeled 6 along its length and 2 along its height. Use the text/diagram dimensions to form the total outside rectangle enclosing beds plus walkways. Its width is 1 + 6 + 1 + 6 + 1 = 15 feet, and its height is 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 10 feet. The whole enclosed area is 15 × 10 = 150 square feet. The six flower beds occupy 6 × (6 × 2) = 72 square feet. Subtract bed area from the whole rectangle: 150 - 72 = 78 square feet of walkway.

claims.claim: The total width of the external large rectangle is 1 + 6 + 1 + 6 + 1 = 15 feet.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: In the horizontal direction there are: left-side walkway 1 foot + left-column flower bed 6 feet + middle walkway 1 foot + right-column flower bed 6 feet + right-side walkway 1 foot, so the total width is 1 + 6 + 1 + 6 + 1 = 15 feet

claims.claim: The total height of the external large rectangle is 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 10 feet.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: In the vertical direction, there are: upper walkway 1 foot + three flower bed heights each 2 feet + two middle walkways each 1 foot + lower walkway 1 foot, so the total height is 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 10 feet

claims.claim: The area of a rectangle equals width multiplied by height.
claims.label: knowledge
claims.source: The area of the entire outer rectangle is 15 × 10 = 150 square feet

claims.claim: The area of the entire outer rectangle is 150 square feet.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The area of the entire outer rectangle is 15 × 10 = 150 square feet

claims.claim: The area of one flower bed is 6 × 2 square feet.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The total area of the six flower beds is 6 × (6 × 2) = 72 square feet

claims.claim: The total area of the six flower beds is 72 square feet.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The total area of the six flower beds is 6 × (6 × 2) = 72 square feet

claims.claim: The walkway area equals the total area minus the flower bed area.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: The walkway area equals the total area minus the flower bed area

claims.claim: The walkway area is 78 square feet.
claims.label: reasoning
claims.source: 150 - 72 = 78 square feet
